name: Ivorian Kedjenou
description: Kedjenou's name literally means 'to shake' in the Baoulé language, and that's exactly the real technique: chicken and vegetables sealed in a canari, a narrow-necked clay pot, with no water added at all, cooked slowly and PERIODICALLY SHAKEN rather than stirred, so the lid never breaks the seal - the dish cooks entirely in its own steam and juices, which is what makes it what it is, not a shortcut stew.
steps_detailed: Combine everything in a heavy pot with a tight-fitting lid, without adding any extra water.

Cover tightly and cook over low heat, shaking the sealed pot occasionally rather than stirring or lifting the lid, 40-45 minutes, until the chicken is tender - real kedjenou depends on this sealed, undisturbed cooking, and the name itself refers to this shaking motion.

name: Ivorian Attieke
description: Attiéké, fermented, granular cassava couscous, is one of Côte d'Ivoire's most iconic staples, traditionally paired with grilled fish - real attiéké's fermentation takes days, so this quicker version approximates the texture without the real tang.
steps_detailed: Steam the grated cassava over simmering water 20-25 minutes, fluffing occasionally with a fork, until it takes on a light, granular, couscous-like texture.

name: Ivorian Garba
description: Garba, fried tuna served over attiéké with a spicy tomato-onion relish, is a beloved Ivorian street food, especially popular as a quick, affordable lunch.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

steps_detailed: Steam the grated cassava 20-22 minutes into attiéké.
Pan-fry the tuna briefly, 2-3 minutes, to warm and lightly crisp.
Simmer the tomatoes, onion, and jalapeño 8-10 minutes into a relish.
Serve the tuna and relish over the attiéké.

name: Ivorian Alloco
description: Alloco, fried ripe plantain served with a spicy onion-tomato sauce, is one of Côte d'Ivoire's most beloved street foods.
steps_detailed: Fry the plantain slices, turning, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply caramelized.
Simmer the tomatoes, onion, and jalapeño 8-10 minutes into a sauce.
Serve the fried plantain topped with the sauce.

name: Ivorian Poulet Braisé (Grilled Chicken)
description: Poulet braisé, grilled chicken marinated in garlic and pepper, a beloved Ivorian street-food staple, often served with alloco.
steps_detailed: Marinate the chicken in the garlic, jalapeño, and lemon juice for at least 20 minutes.
Grill, turning, 12-15 minutes, until charred and cooked through.

name: Ivorian Sauce Graine
description: Sauce graine, a rich palm-fruit-based stew, is one of Côte d'Ivoire's most beloved sauces - real palm fruit isn't a distinct item here, so this leans on tomato and peanut for a similarly rich, reddish base, though it's honestly missing palm fruit's own distinct waxy richness.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter with the tomatoes and a little water, then add to the pot.
Simmer 20-22 minutes until the chicken is tender.

name: Ivorian Foutou
description: Foutou, plantain and cassava pounded together into a smooth, stretchy dough, a beloved Ivorian staple, traditionally torn by hand to scoop up sauce.
steps_detailed: Boil the plantain and cassava together until completely soft, 20-25 minutes.
Pound vigorously until smooth and stretchy.

name: Ivorian Placali
description: Placali, a smooth, stretchy fermented cassava paste, a genuine Ivorian staple closely related to Ghanaian banku.
steps_detailed: Mix the grated cassava with water and let ferment at room temperature 24 hours.
Cook the fermented mixture over medium heat, stirring constantly, 15-18 minutes, until thick and stretchy.

name: Ivorian Egusi Soup
description: Egusi soup, thickened with real ground melon seeds, is shared with Nigeria and found throughout much of West Africa, including Côte d'Ivoire.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.
Mix the egusi with water into a paste and fry in spoonfuls, 5-6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and beef, and simmer 10-12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach in the last 3 minutes.

Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

Fry the egg separately and serve on top.

Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, turning, 4-5 minutes, until deeply golden.
